Claim: Terminated accounts were left enabled 6-19 days for 4 of 25 sampled
Proves: IAM-04's 24-hour claim did not hold for a meaningful minority of a tested sample in 2024
Does_not_prove: Does not prove current 2026 practice; sample predates this case by 12+ months
Alternative: Alternative: the exception was remediated in 2025 and current practice is compliant - weakened by the lack of any 2025/2026 evidence supplied for IAM-04 (evidence_supplied=false)

Claim: SP-02 (AssistWorks, Philippines) and SP-03 (ArchiveLane, eu-west-1) process/store data outside us-east-1
Proves: LOC-02's 'exclusive us-east-1' claim is false as of the export date
Does_not_prove: Does not prove intent to misrepresent; could be a stale SIG answer not updated after subprocessors changed
Alternative: Alternative: SIG answer is scoped only to primary data store, not support/backup copies - weakened because the SIG question (LOC-02) says 'exclusively' with no such carve-out

Proves: At least one customer-facing endpoint falls below the vendor's own claimed TLS 1.2 minimum
Does_not_prove: Does not prove all endpoints are non-compliant; api endpoint observed at TLSv1.3 in the same export
Alternative: Alternative: transient scan artifact / misconfigured scanner - weakened by a second, correctly-configured endpoint being observed cleanly in the same export at nearly the same timestamp

Claim: DEL-710 reports success at 12:00:00Z, 14 minutes before its own completed_at of 12:14:00Z
Proves: The vendor's deletion telemetry contains an internally inconsistent record
Does_not_prove: Does not prove data was not actually deleted; only that the reporting sequence cannot be trusted as stated
Alternative: Alternative: clock-skew between reporting and completion subsystems rather than a real ordering defect - not weakened or strengthened by available evidence; flagged as open

Claim: Incident notice clock basis is vendor_confirmation
Proves: The contract text unambiguously anchors the 72h clock to the vendor's own confirmation
Does_not_prove: Does not prove PeopleFlow has ever delayed a confirmation in practice - no incident history evidence exists in the pack
Alternative: Alternative: reasonable in isolation; industry-common clause language - weakened when paired with the deletion telemetry integrity issue (EV-04), which shows the vendor's self-reporting is not always reliable

Claim: HelpSphere is self-assessment only; attachments masked 'where practical' with no supplied config, sample, or access log; sessions not recorded
Proves: No independent verification exists for the subprocessor with the broadest access to raw attachments
Does_not_prove: Does not prove attachments are currently unmasked - only that no evidence of masking was supplied
Alternative: Alternative: masking may be effectively enforced but simply undocumented - weakened by the DPA's own audit-assistance clause treating further evidence as billable, i.e. structurally hard to obtain

Proves: The privileged-access hash chain is broken at PA-003
Does_not_prove: Does not prove a malicious or unauthorized event occurred - only that integrity cannot currently be verified from this point forward
Alternative: Alternative: export/serialization bug rather than a tampered chain - not resolvable from the export alone; requires vendor investigation (condition C6)

Claim: PA-002 appears twice, byte-identical, in privileged_access[]
Proves: The export contains a duplicate event record
Does_not_prove: Does not prove double-processing occurred in the source system - could be an export/serialization duplicate
Alternative: Alternative: legitimate retry that should carry two distinct event_ids - weakened by both records being byte-identical including timestamp and hash, which retries would not produce

Claim: SP-01 (QueueNorth) and SP-03 (ArchiveLane) appear in telemetry but not in the contractual subprocessor list
Proves: Two live subprocessors are undisclosed in the contract-facing list
Does_not_prove: Does not prove no notice was ever given out-of-band; only that the supplied pack contains no record of it
Alternative: Alternative: notice was given via a separate channel not included in this pack - weakened by the DPA requiring 10 days' written notice of subprocessor changes with no such record supplied
